label: copy-phase p input early in a long copy, before outputting p/o
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is p (100% of activations). It never fires on p during the original phase or at the delimiter. Activity sits near the start of the copy (recall_idx 1-3, about 99% of mass) and gets stronger in longer sequences (L=9 holds 54% of mass, none at L<=4). Magnitude is highest when the next output is p or o (out_tok p holds 51% of mass, o 21%); top examples are p followed by o or by p. However, copy-phase p at recall_idx<=3 has low precision (~4%) unless the output is restricted to p/o, and that restriction loses about 30% of mass, which is weak firing before other outputs. So the predicate captures the core but is incomplete on both precision and recall.
